children: Saudi renewables company Acwa said commercial operations have commenced at the $1.8 billion Red Sea multi-utilities project.

Marafiq Red Sea for Energy Company (Marafiq) - the project company formed by Acwa, SPIC Huanghe Hydropower and Saudi Tabreed and by The Red Sea Utilities Company, a subsidiary of Red Sea Global, has signed the project commercial operation date for “the world’s largest off-grid renewable utilities system”, commencing the 25-year concession.
The consortium provides renewable power, potable water, wastewater treatment, district cooling, and waste management to the Red Sea project, Acwa said in a statement.
Financial close was announced in February 2022, with $1.33 billion in senior debt facilities, funded by Saudi and international banks.
The utility system was engineered and constructed by SEPCO III (Shandong Tiejun consortium) as EPC contractor and is operated and maintained by Acwa.

Generation comes from a 340 MWac solar photovoltaic (PV) plant working alongside a 1,227 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS). The generating system delivers up to 760,000 MWh of clean energy a year, avoiding around 600,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide over the same period.

The scope of the project also covers the construction of three seawater reverse osmosis plants, a waste management center and a sewage treatment plant that will allow 16,000 cubic metres per day of waste. Additionally, district cooling totaling 32,500 refrigeration tonnes (RT) is provided to the hotels and the airport.

All utility services underwent rigorous environmental and social impact assessment processes and received the requisite permits from the National Center for Environmental Compliance, the statement said.

In addition, these services remain subject to Marafiq continuous environmental compliance and monitoring, ensuring ongoing compliance and management of the surrounding marine and terrestrial ecosystems.
